title: Fusion and hot-break books
summary: Fusion is a marriage made in hell; pattern books.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: So you know, that's the stuff you hear. WRVR, I wish you could get an injunction against them because they say 'Jazz has never sounded better,' and they do what they call fusion, fusion between disco and jazz. I want to tell you, that's a marriage made in hell. That's like mating a goat with a ferris wheel.

And you know, think of all the kids listening to this and saying, oh, that's heavy (humming). And that's all they do, a pentatonic scale and they've got these mathematical patterns. I've got books for those. They write books with all these patterns you can practice. And you can buy them anyplace. When I was a kid they had Louis Armstrong's book of 100 Hot Breaks, Red Nichol's 100 Hot Breaks and Whole Tone Scales, you can apply these anyplace. And we're right back to that. And they're stuck and nobody ever did it and I wish nobody did it now. But they're doing it now.
Now they've got their books of hot breaks, and memorizing these things. And laying them on top of you.
